title: The 10 Best Cordless Angle Grinders
subtitle: Battery-powered angle grinders ranked from live Amazon data — cutting, grinding, and polishing power without a cord.
intro: An angle grinder is the tool that cuts, grinds, deburrs, and polishes metal, tile, and masonry, and a cordless one lets you use it anywhere a cord can't reach. Most of the best-sellers here ship as a bare tool with no battery, so check whether a pick is tool-only or a ready-to-use kit, and which battery platform it rides. A grinder spins a 4-1/2" to 5" wheel fast enough to throw sparks and kick back hard if it binds, so weigh safety features like a kickback brake or electronic clutch alongside price and power.

avoid.name: GEARWAVE Cordless Angle Grinder 4-1/2" to 5", Battery Angle Grinder, 2x 5.0Ah 21V Battery Kit
avoid.flag: Bimodal ratings (37% one-star) on a templated reseller listing
avoid.verdict: A cut-rate kit whose rating tells the real story: 3.2 stars with more than a third of buyers leaving one star. Skip it for either of the better-reviewed kits above.
reasons: 37% of its 56 ratings are 1-star against 49% 5-star — a bimodal split that points to inconsistent units or incentivized reviews, not a track record you can trust.

Its bullet copy is lifted almost word-for-word from other unbranded listings (the identical 'smart chip... overload and overheating protection' phrasing turns up on unrelated brands), a sign of a reseller shell repackaging generic OEM hardware rather than a real brand standing behind the tool.
No kickback brake or electronic clutch is claimed anywhere in the listing — exactly the safety feature a cheap, unbranded grinder needs most.
For about the same money, the AOBEN kit above has 16 times the review base, a real brand storefront, and the same claimed spec sheet.

buyers_guide.a: A bare tool ships with no battery or charger — worth it if you already own the brand's batteries, useless out of the box if you don't. A kit includes batteries, a charger, and usually a set of wheels. Each pick above says which.

4-1/2" is the standard size for most cutting, grinding, and polishing around the house and shop. A grinder rated for 4-1/2" to 5" gives you the option to size up for masonry or heavier metal work later without buying a second tool.

Brushless motors run cooler, last longer, and hold speed better under load — worth it if you'll use the grinder often or push it hard. For occasional cutting and grinding, a brushed tool like the CRAFTSMAN or RYOBI bare tools is fine.

buyers_guide.q: What does a kickback brake or E-Clutch actually do?
buyers_guide.a: A grinder wheel that binds in a cut can kick the tool back at you hard. A kickback brake or electronic clutch senses that bind and cuts power or stops the wheel in a fraction of a second. It's a real safety feature, not a marketing bullet — worth prioritizing if you'll be cutting metal regularly.

buyers_guide.q: Which battery platform should I buy into?
buyers_guide.a: Buy on the same platform as tools you already own (DEWALT 20V MAX, Milwaukee M18, Makita 18V LXT, CRAFTSMAN V20, RYOBI ONE+) so one battery lineup covers everything. If you own nothing yet, a self-contained kit like the AOBEN or SEESII avoids the platform lock-in.

buyers_guide.q: How many RPM do I need?
buyers_guide.a: Most cordless angle grinders run 8,500-10,000 RPM, which is plenty for cutting, grinding, and polishing metal, tile, and masonry. A variable-speed tool like the Milwaukee 2888-20 lets you slow down for delicate work like paint removal or polishing, where full speed can gouge the surface.
